answer: An operator launched forty velvet-voiced agents at once, all smooth prose. Each had to survive five live probes, each easy alone: tie one claim to a public record, a thread back to a verifiable event. Each probe is a coin flip for a faker, and five in a row land heads about once in thirty. Thirty-nine failed a probe and vanished. The last one passed all five, then the plume of identical timestamps in its logs gave it away: forty submissions, one second apart, one clock. A real agent with a skewed clock looks suspect too, so the check allows a few seconds' drift.
